sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
**Sources (no sell-side data):** FY26 Q4 earnings press release, microsoft.com/Investor (Azure +43% cc, Microsoft Cloud $59.3B +27%, RPO +84% to $678B, capex $115.9B FY26); FY2026 annual statements (ended 2026-06-30), $B.

**EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS gate:** Accruals (NI−CFO)/avg assets FY26 = (133.7−182.9)/688.7 = −7.1% — CFO runs ahead of NI, no flag. No AR/rev divergence; inventory immaterial. SBC $12.4B = 3.7% of revenue, real cost, subtracted below. Watch (not manipulation): reported FCF fell to $67.0B from $71.6B as capex doubled — the EPS(+32%)/FCF divergence is the thesis's central question (kill criteria). Gate clears.

**Revenue build (segment, $B):** FY26 $331.8 total (+18%): PBP ~$135, Intelligent Cloud ~$145 (Azure +43% cc in Q4), MPC ~$52 (Q4 −4%). Deliberate forward decel: FY27E $388 (+17%), FY28E $444 (+14.5%), FY29E $502 (+13%); Azure modeled 43%→~33%→~28%→~25% cc. Margin ~47% held through FY29E (op income $155.2B FY26; the Q4 dip to 45.1% is depreciation timing, not opex). **EBIT $182B/$209B/$236B FY27-29E; NOPAT (19% tax) $147B/$169B/$191B.**

**Reinvestment math (method step 1):** net capex ($115.9 − D&A $38.5) ≈ $77B on NOPAT $125.7B → reinvestment ~61%; ROIC ≈ 125.7/(equity $442.4 + net debt $19.4) ≈ 27%. g = 0.61×0.27 ≈ 16.5%, matching the +17.8% print — growth is manufactured at a franchise ROIC, not declared.

**Owner earnings (step 5):** OCF $182.9B − maintenance capex (~$22B; the excess ~$94B is the AI growth buildout) − SBC $12.4B ≈ **$148B (~$20/sh)**. The punitive $67B reported-FCF view treats all capex as current cost; honest owner earnings sit between — the gap is the bet.

**Fair value / 3-assumption sensitivity:** 9% COE (house USD band), fade by ~year 10, terminal g 3.5%. Value-critical assumptions: (1) Azure path — bull +30%+ cc through FY28 (RPO visibility), base ~25% by FY29, bear high-teens: ±$120; (2) capex plateau — buildout done by FY28 lifts FCF conversion ~39%→~60%; a spiral >$130B slips it forever (kpi kill); (3) exit multiple — fade-to-COE 15x→$363; 20x with lift→~$576; 22x→~$710. Target $700 sits just under the top bracket and implies 21.7x exit EV/EBIT — a **de-rating** from today's 25x on FY26: no multiple expansion (survival test passed).

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.detail: one sentence, from memory, written before document work
sections.markdown: What I believe the market narrative is: MSFT is the consensus "safe mega-cap AI compounder" — Azure re-accelerating (43%), RPO +84%, and under CAUTIOUS the Street is crowding into it as the default quality long, which is why it ran +41% in six months; whether that run is spent sentiment or the market paying near what booked growth is worth.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** (a) the +41% six-month run already repriced the re-acceleration — buy-the-dip is consensus (55 analysts, Strong Buy, average target ~+11% over spot), "everyone already owns it"; (b) MSFT is expensive at 28.8x trailing / ~26x forward with FCF actually DOWN year-over-year, so the multiple must compress.

**Why wrong:** The run is only six months old and the de-rating frame is stale: on trailing earnings the multiple FELL from ~38x a year ago to ~29x today because EPS grew 32% while price was flat (mom12 −1.9%) — the 12m window IS the compression; the re-rating leg (mom6 +41.6%) has only reclaimed part of it, and forward PE ~26x sits at the low end of MSFT's decade (28-40x). Meanwhile the re-acceleration is contract-booked, not hoped-for: RPO +84% to $678B and Azure +43% cc are in the quarterly binders — the strongest order book in company history — and the compounding math is real (g ≈ 0.61×0.27 ≈ 17%, matching the print). Variant: the market prices the FCF-conversion TIMING (capex doubled, FCF flat) at a below-history multiple while the contract book grew 84%. Our target needs the multiple to FALL, not expand.

**What proves us wrong:** Observable, each this half: Azure cc  ~$130B with FCF still flat (spiral, no conversion lift); or EPS missing ~$24 FY27E while ~26x forward holds (the "low multiple" was fair because growth was lower quality than the RPO suggests). Any one falsifies.

**Edge taxonomy:** (a) analytical — multiple-survival discipline on a consensus-strong-buy name (target implies exit EV/EBIT 21.7x, BELOW today's 25x-on-FY26) with paid-for growth verified via reinvestment × ROIIC; (c) time-arbitrage — the market trades quarter-to-quarter FCF prints while the 2-4y contract book (RPO $678B) makes 2026-2028 revenue the most visible in MSFT's history. Not (b)/(d). Deliberate gap-fill: the GLOBAL sleeve was all-extended semis/rates; MSFT is the quality-compounder balance under CAUTIOUS. Honest EV is thin (+2.2% over 3y) — a quality/diversification fill, sized small, not a fat edge; we say so plainly.

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is September-2029 and this position lost ~30%. The most likely reason is the archetype's named dominant failure: a **structural de-rating masquerading as a cyclical one**. Azure growth didn't fade to ~25% — it fell to high-teens as hyperscaler/BYOAI capacity commoditized AI-cloud economics and export-control churn hit the AI GPU book; capex never plateaued, FCF stayed flat while EPS compounded, and the market concluded the ~$116B annual buildout was margin-dilutive — the forward multiple walked from 26x toward the fade-to-COE ~$363 and the kill fired near $354. Secondary: pure macro — a hiking Fed / DXY ~100.8 compressing long-duration multiples broadly, de-rating MSFT with the market despite intact fundamentals. Either way the honest lesson: we bought at consensus's price (entry within 3% of the printed high) a thin-edge diversifier, and when the multiple broke, growth carried the P&L but not the price.
